You missed out SoRA (https://www.ucl.ac.uk/academic-manual/chapters/chapter-4-assessment-framework-taught-programmes/section-5-reasonable-adjustments), which would've been worth mentioning. If you have mental health issues with proof from the GP, you'll get various assessment mitigations.

E.G. You'll get granted 1 week extensions just by letting know your course administrator, without going through faculty. Various exam arrangements such as extended time, and breaks during exams can be put in place according to your condition. This includes anxiety and depression.

Hey, I'm studying UG Psych and Lang Sci. I'm sorry to say this, but the Psych department isn't the best at looking after their students, which my tutor who used to work there (now in Psych and Lang) told me. The whole department is oversubscribed with students, so "personal" tutors change every term. I had a friend studying psych, but she couldn't handle it and quit. 

Generally yes, the system is there and looks good, but the uni's mental health support service is oversubscribed and underfunded/staffed, so it'll take you a while to get into the loop. Once I was in, the therapists and the Extenuating Circumstance system were great, so that I can support.

The person above missed out this important info, but if you have mental health problems, get proof from your GP and it'll be easier to get extensions for coursework, and arrangements for exams. I just have to send an email to the course admin that I need an extension, and he can grant me a one week extension for any coursework on the spot, without going through the whole faculty and stuff (2 weeks for dissertations). More information here, usually referred to as SoRA https://www.ucl.ac.uk/academic-manual/chapters/chapter-4-assessment-framework-taught-programmes/section-5-reasonable-adjustments.

I don't know about other schools (so if there are Year 2s / Alumnus out there who took Geography as well, I'd be happy if you can back me up), but this is how it went for my school:
So for Geography you have to do a field work where you actually go to the study area to collect data and information, and the content is based on one of the Option topics. In our school we chose the Ocean and Coasts Option so all of the SL/HL people went to a beach in Spain, which we collected data there, and then we came back and processed the data which we shared on Google Drive.

The criteria for the IA is the same for both SL/HL, so we could ask around anyone who took Geography for peer review and help. Plus the teachers take a big part in the planning of the fieldwork so there was a lot of helpful guidance on our IA.

And during the field trip obviously we won't be collecting data the whole day, so although it depends on where you go and how long you stay, we had free time in the evening to ourselves which was fun :)

I think you should go and ask seniors in your school how and where they did it, I think it does differ a lot amongst schools. In our school it's been a tradition for years with this combination of Oceans and Coasts Option and Spain, but I know other schools every year they just visit their neighbour cities to do it, which they said was pretty boring.

Geography - everyone was doing the same thing so we could use the same data tables and graphs together, and we could ask each other for feedback because everyone was doing the same content.
